modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Smell / 嗅觉
paragraphs: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为嗅觉。你可以观察，一个地方的气息与整体氛围，是否会让你先注意到差异，再逐渐找到描述它的语言。例如，比较两个熟悉的工作空间，把空气、噪声、光线和分心因素分别记录下来。最初的印象可以提出问题，却不能证明某个地方或某个人安全与否。
如果一种感受会影响重要选择，可以进一步问：哪些条件发生了变化？换一个环境后，感觉是否相同？还有哪些资料没有取得？嗅觉分类不代表能够识别疾病、谎言或他人的隐秘动机。涉及安全与健康时，仍须采用实际证据及相应专业意见。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Smell / 嗅觉
paragraphs: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Smell. You can explore whether the atmosphere of a place helps you notice distinctions before you can explain them. For example, compare two familiar working spaces and record the concrete differences in air, noise, light and distraction. A first impression can open a question; it cannot establish that a place or person is safe or unsafe.

When an impression matters, translate it into conditions that can be checked. Ask what changed, whether another setting gives the same impression and what information is still missing. Smell does not establish an ability to detect disease, dishonesty or hidden intentions. Use ordinary safety guidance and relevant expertise for those decisions.

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
paragraphs: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为味觉。你可以从直接体验中的细微区别来探索这一主题：先尝试一个可逆的小选择，注意它与另一种选择具体有什么不同，再决定是否继续。例如，比较两种工具或两份作品时，把自己重视的细节说清楚，会比只说好或不好更有帮助。
个人偏好不是衡量品质的普遍标准。可以把喜欢的特点与任务要求分开，也容许别人有不同偏好。这一阅读不提供食物、饮食或医疗处方，更不把一时喜欢当成作出重大承诺的充分依据。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Taste / 味觉
paragraphs: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Taste. A useful way to explore this theme is through careful distinctions in direct experience: trying a small, reversible option, noticing what actually differs and deciding what deserves another attempt. Comparing two versions of a tool or a piece of work can make your preferences more specific than simply calling one good and the other bad.

Personal preference is not a universal measure of quality. Name the feature you value, compare it with the requirements of the task and allow other people to have different preferences. This reading does not prescribe food, a diet or a medical regimen, and it does not make a momentary liking sufficient evidence for a major commitment.

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Outer Vision / 外在视觉
paragraphs: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为外在视觉。你可以观察，可见的排列如何帮助自己理解一件事：看一张图、比较具体样例，或把有关对象放在能够看清关系的位置。一幅共同绘制的草图，也可能让参与者发现，大家原先想象的其实不是同一个问题。
容易看见的内容不一定就是全部事实。需要把画面中的模式与日期、定义及画面之外的资料比较。外表不能单独证明他人的动机，也不能预测结果。图示可以帮助提出问题，并应在证据变化时接受修正。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Outer Vision / 外在视觉
paragraphs: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Outer Vision. You can explore how visible arrangements help you understand a situation: seeing a diagram, comparing examples or placing the relevant objects where their relationships can be examined. A shared sketch can also reveal that two people have been imagining different versions of the same problem.

What is easy to see is not necessarily the whole story. Compare the visible pattern with dates, definitions and information that is absent from the picture. Appearance alone cannot establish another person’s motives or predict an outcome. Use a visual reference to support inquiry, then revise it when the evidence changes.

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 内在视觉：当理解先在你的内部形成画面
paragraphs: 你的人类图在 Cognition（认知感官）这一层，对应 Inner Vision（内在视觉）。这组传统分类把阅读带向一种与内部图像和整体印象有关的经验：有时，别人还在逐项说明一件事情，你的理解却可能先以画面、空间关系或某种完整场景的形式逐渐成形。你可能更容易先想象一件事情完成后的轮廓，再回头寻找组成它的步骤；也可能在安静下来之后，才发现白天接收到的零散信息开始彼此连接。对你来说，一项认识未必总是从第一句话开始建立，有时候它先是一幅还没有被完全说清楚的内部地图。

这种方式可以在学习、创作和解决问题时提供另一种切入点。例如，当你准备调整一项工作流程，脑海中可能先出现不同部门如何交接、哪些环节互相影响的整体图景。你知道自己想要改善什么，却未必马上知道怎样把它解释给别人。此时，把想法画成流程、安排成步骤，或借助具体例子向别人说明，能够让内部形成的理解逐渐进入可以讨论和检验的现实。你的优势不一定只是拥有画面，而是能够在适当的时候，将它整理成别人也能参与的表达方式。

你也可能注意到，持续受到声音、讯息或他人要求打断时，自己不容易完成这个整理过程。有些想法需要一段不必立即回应的时间，才有机会发展出更清楚的结构。你可以在条件允许时，先记录脑海中出现的关键词、关系或草图，再决定哪些值得继续研究。但也不需要强迫自己一定看见清晰影像：有些人体验到的是空间关系、顺序感或整体印象。无论呈现方式如何，内部形成的画面与直觉都可以是探索的起点，重要的判断仍要回到实际证据、相关人的反馈和可验证的结果。
当 Inner Vision 与你其他已确认的配置一起阅读时，它可以帮助你更具体地认识：什么情况下想法会自然成形，什么时候适合把它转换为语言，以及哪些认识值得进一步投入实践。你不必急于把每个内部画面变成行动，也不必因为别人暂时不明白，就否定自己的理解。让内部形成的想法拥有恰当的表达和验证过程，正是这项认知主题可以进入日常生活的方式。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Inner Vision: When Understanding Takes Shape Within You
paragraphs: Your Human Design Cognition is classified as Inner Vision. In the traditional framework, this brings attention to the way images, spatial relationships and an overall sense of a situation may take shape internally. At times, other people may still be explaining a problem step by step while you are beginning to imagine how its parts belong together. You might picture the eventual outcome before knowing exactly how to describe the path toward it, or discover that disconnected details begin to make more sense once you have a quieter moment to consider them. Understanding does not always begin as a complete sentence. Sometimes it starts as an internal outline that has yet to find its language.

This perspective may feel especially relevant when you are learning, creating or improving a process. Imagine reviewing a workflow that involves several people. You might first form an overall impression of how information moves between them and where the sequence could be simpler. Explaining that picture to others is a separate task. A sketch, a process map or a concrete example can help translate what you have imagined into something that other people can examine and test. The potential strength is not merely having an internal image, but learning when and how to make that understanding accessible and useful.

You may also notice that constant interruptions leave little room to organize an impression fully. Sometimes a short interval without new demands is enough to return to an idea with more clarity. Writing down relationships, drawing a rough diagram or revisiting a question later may provide a helpful bridge. You do not need to force yourself to see vivid mental pictures: for some people, the experience may be closer to recognizing an arrangement, a sequence or a whole. Whatever form it takes, an internal impression can be a starting point for exploration; reliable conclusions still benefit from evidence, feedback and practical testing.

Read alongside the other verified elements of your chart, Inner Vision can offer a more personal way to consider when ideas begin to cohere, how you communicate them and which possibilities deserve further attention. You do not have to turn every inner picture into a task or assume that a lack of immediate agreement makes your understanding less valuable. Allowing an idea to develop, find clear expression and meet reality gives this theme a practical place in everyday life.

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
paragraphs: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为感觉。你可以从一段体验的整体感受来探索它：某种节奏、环境或互动，是否让自己更安定、紧绷或容易分心。把当时的条件与感受一起记录，能够帮助区别持续存在的因素与某一次困难的时刻。
感受值得被注意，但不必因此成为不可质疑的判断。可以同时比较睡眠、工作量、预期及现实任务要求。重要选择仍须结合内在权威的过程、可靠资料和适当意见。这一分类不诊断身体状况，也不证明能够直接读取别人的情绪。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Feeling / 感觉
paragraphs: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Feeling. This can be explored as attention to the overall felt quality of an experience: whether a pace, setting or interaction leaves you more settled, strained or distracted. Recording the circumstances alongside the feeling helps distinguish a recurring condition from a difficult moment.

A feeling deserves attention without becoming an unquestionable verdict. Compare sleep, workload, expectations and the practical demands of the situation. For important decisions, combine your chart’s Authority process with reliable information and appropriate advice. This classification does not diagnose a condition or establish that you can read another person’s emotions.

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Touch / 触觉
paragraphs: 你的 Cognition 在传统分类中称为触觉。你可以观察，亲手接触材料、试用工具，或实际演练一个步骤，是否能帮助自己理解说明文字没有说清楚的地方。一次简短试用，可能让握持、阻力或空间安排中真正影响工作的问题变得具体。
直接接触也有边界。须尊重他人的同意与安全，不把碰触人或物品当成取得隐藏信息的方式。可以描述实际注意到的内容，再与其他证据比较。如果不适合直接操作，应采用可及的替代方式，而不是把分类变成必须照做的要求。

modules.lineage: SEC10.07 successor under explicit owner correction
modules.title: 10.7 Touch / 触觉
paragraphs: Your Cognition is traditionally described as Touch. You can explore whether handling a material, trying a device or physically rehearsing a task helps clarify what a description leaves uncertain. A short practical trial may reveal the grip, resistance or arrangement that matters for the actual work.

Direct contact has boundaries. Respect consent and safety, and do not assume that touching a person or object reveals hidden information. Describe what you actually noticed and compare it with other evidence. Where direct handling is unavailable or unsuitable, use an accessible alternative rather than treating the classification as a requirement.
